Beating Visor Fog on British Roads

Visor fogging is every UK rider's nemesis. Our damp climate creates perfect condensation conditions that can obscure vision at the worst possible moments. Whether crawling through Cotswolds morning mist or riding through rain on the A82, a fog-free visor is essential for safe touring.

Why Visors Fog

Fogging occurs when warm breath hits the cooler inner visor surface. Moisture condenses into tiny droplets that scatter light and reduce visibility. It worsens in cold weather, at low speeds where airflow cannot clear moisture, and when the visor is sealed against rain — exactly the conditions UK riders face most often.

Pinlock Inserts: The Gold Standard

A Pinlock insert is a secondary lens inside your visor held by two pins at either edge. The air gap acts as a thermal barrier preventing the inner surface from reaching dew point temperature. The insert has a moisture-absorbing coating that captures residual condensation before it can obscure vision.

  • Pinlock 30 — Basic anti-fog for dry mild conditions. Not recommended for UK touring.
  • Pinlock 70 — Enhanced protection suitable for most UK riding situations.
  • Pinlock 120 — Maximum protection with four times the absorption capacity. Essential for all-weather touring in British conditions.

Fitting a Pinlock Insert

Most modern touring helmets are Pinlock-ready with two pins on the visor. Flex the insert slightly, hook one pin, then push onto the second. It should sit flat with an even air gap around the perimeter. If it bows outward or touches the visor, adjust pin positions by rotating the pins.

Alternative Anti-Fog Solutions

  • Anti-fog sprays — Apply a hydrophilic coating that prevents droplets forming. Effective but requires reapplication every few rides.
  • Anti-fog wipes — Convenient single-use wipes. Keep several in your tank bag for mid-tour reapplication at fuel stops.
  • Breath deflectors — Nose guards redirect exhaled air downward away from the visor. Effective combined with other treatments.
A fogged visor is a genuine safety hazard, not just an inconvenience. Invest in a Pinlock 120 insert and replace it annually. Your vision and your safety are worth every penny.

Visor Care Tips

Never clean Pinlock inserts with alcohol-based cleaners which strip the moisture-absorbing coating. Use only warm water and a soft cloth. Store in the protective pouch when not in use. Replace if scratched, yellowed, or no longer absorbing effectively. With proper care a Pinlock 120 lasts a full touring season of regular use.
keyTakeaways: Fogging happens when warm breath condenses on the cooler inner visor, worst in cold, damp, slow-speed UK conditions.
A Pinlock insert creates a sealed air gap plus a moisture-absorbing coating to keep the inner surface clear.
Choose Pinlock 120 for all-weather British touring; Pinlock 30 is inadequate for our climate.
Never clean Pinlock inserts with alcohol-based cleaners, which strip the absorbent coating.
Anti-fog sprays, wipes and breath deflectors work as backups but need regular reapplication.

faq.q: Which Pinlock grade do I need in the UK?
faq.a: For British all-weather touring choose the Pinlock 120, which has roughly four times the moisture absorption of the basic Pinlock 30 and stays clear in prolonged cold, wet conditions. The Pinlock 70 suits most general riding, while the Pinlock 30 is only adequate for dry, mild days and is not recommended for UK touring where damp fogging is a constant challenge.

faq.q: How do I fit a Pinlock insert?
faq.a: Most modern touring visors are Pinlock-ready with two adjustable pins. Flex the insert slightly, hook it onto one pin, then push it onto the second so it sits flat with an even air gap around the edge. If it bows outward or touches the visor, rotate the eccentric pins to adjust tension until the silicone bead seals evenly all the way round.

faq.q: How do I clean and care for the insert?
faq.a: Use only warm water and a soft cloth, never alcohol-based cleaners, which strip the moisture-absorbing coating. Store the insert in its protective pouch when removed to prevent scratches. Replace it if it becomes scratched, yellowed or stops absorbing effectively. With careful cleaning a Pinlock 120 will last a full touring season of regular use.

faq.q: What if my visor is not Pinlock-ready?
faq.a: Then rely on anti-fog treatments: hydrophilic sprays and single-use wipes coat the inner surface to stop droplets forming, though they need reapplying every few rides. A breath deflector or chin curtain that redirects exhaled air downward helps considerably when combined with a treatment. Carrying a few anti-fog wipes in your tank bag lets you refresh the coating at fuel stops.
